Principal finding: TAEC enforces at most one valid update per neighbour per cycle, rejects messages older than Smax=5, and triggers aggregation only when participation meets the threshold.
Evidence: Sections 3.2–3.4; Algorithm 1; protocol-level enforcement in all runs.
Limit of interpretation: Defines contribution and freshness bounds; end-to-end traffic and wall-clock efficiency were not measured.

Principal finding: ARC-Trust+ obtains higher mean Macro-F1 than distance filtering alone on four of five datasets under sign-flip + stealth drift. Under Gaussian noise, canary-only is highest on four datasets. Across the five drift regimes, ARC-Trust+ Macro-F1 varies by at most 0.031 within each dataset.
Limit of interpretation: Relative gains depend on traffic distribution and attack type. Temporal residuals govern update weighting, not standalone Byzantine isolation.

Principal finding: Isolation recall = 1.000 and false-isolation rate = 0.000 across all five datasets and three attack types; mean Byzantine trust remains below τiso=0.35.
Limit of interpretation: Isolation depends on the presence of the cryptographic canary in the evaluated threat model. The independent isolation capacity of SPD geometry without the canary remains unverified.
